messages:
ashley: Heads up, seeing a spike of Pending GPU pods in eu-west-1-gpu pool. Several services stalled with `0/40 nodes are available: 40 Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu` but cluster still has free fractional/MIG capacity.
mike: can you paste kubectl describe on one of the pending pods?
ashley: sure, here's the main error from `kubectl describe pod api-infer-77f6c`:

Events:
  Type     Reason             Age                From              Message
  ----     ------             ----               ----              -------
  Warning  FailedScheduling   2m (x9 over 7m)    default-scheduler  0/40 nodes are available: 40 Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu

ashley: our nodepools are mixed: 8x A100-80GB nodes, 24x A100-40GB nodes with MIG profiles enabled, and a few smaller T4 pools. Pod requests are `nvidia.com/gpu: 0.25` via MIG slices.
lena: sounds like autoscaler chose to scale up T4s instead of adding another A100-40GB, so slices can't pack nicely. autoscaler-bot, what scale activity happened around 1987654300?
autoscaler-bot: ScaleUp: group eu-west1-a-a100-40gb increased from 4 -> 6 at 1987654312. ScaleUp: group eu-west1-b-t4-small increased from 6 -> 9 at 1987654318.
nate: ok that's the problem — CA used the default expander (random/most-pods) and picked the cheaper T4 group. T4s don't expose the same MIG profiles we rely on, so fractional requests get rejected.
kevin: quick check: `kubectl get nodes -o=custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,GPU:.status.allocatable.nvidia.com/gpu,labels:.metadata.labels` shows the T4 pool has `nvidia.com/gpu=1` but no mig.gpu.alpha.kubernetes.io/profiles label.
ashley: so pods request `nvidia.com/gpu:0.25` (MIG-profile matching) and device-plugin can't satisfy on T4 -> scheduler treats as insufficient GPUs even though total numeric GPU exists.
mike: two action items: 1) change cluster-autoscaler expander to prefer A100-40gb group (e.g., `--expander=priority` with priority config) or set node-group priority. 2) add scale-up filter to prefer groups with mig label or same GPU type.
lena: we can also set CA flag `--balance-similar-node-groups=false` to avoid mixing incompatible flavors during scale-up bursts, but that may increase cost/latency.
nate: alternative: add a scheduler predicate webhook that prefers nodes with label `gpu.mig=true` for pods requesting <1 GPU, quick hack while we tune CA.
kevin: another immediate mitigation: set a temporary PDB + eviction for low-priority batch jobs to free contiguous slices for inference pods.
ashley: I pushed a k8s taint to T4 pool: `kubectl taint nodes -l nodepool=t4 gpu.slice-incompatible=true:NoSchedule` to force CA to stop filling T4s with MIG-sliced pods; will monitor.
autoscaler-bot: ScaleDown: group eu-west1-b-t4-small decreased from 9 -> 7 at 1987654364.
mike: nice. Long term we should update autoscaler NodeGroup config with `scaleUpPriority` and add node affinity in pod templates: `nodeSelector: gpu-type: a100-40` for latency-critical services.
lena: also file for infra backlog: add feature request to CA to respect custom node labels when choosing groups for fractional-GPU workloads. I'll create a ticket.
ashley: thanks — after the taint a batch of Pending pods moved to Running, but a couple still stuck. I'll run `kubectl describe` on those and loop back. :thumbsup:
mike: if any pods remain stuck after 10m, escalate to runtime team. Might be a device-plugin bug with new mig operator version.
ashley: noted, will follow up in this thread with final status.
